messages:
ashley: Heads-up: tonight in eu-west-1 three dedicated slices triggered sustained egress bursts (~2Gbps each) that caused ToR queueing. GPUs were fine but hosted latency spiked for a few routes.

dan: seeing the same in metrics — net_tx for rack-7 jumped. autoscaler didn't react because CPU/GPU usage stayed normal. dsh logs show repeated multipart uploads after generation finished.

infra-bot: alert: egress_saturation_euwest_3 triggered at 1739123560 — TOC drop rate > 5% for 4m.

samir: my read: customers are doing large post-processing (embeddings dump + upload) from dedicated slices. outputs are heavy and sent off-cluster (S3/cdn).

lee: our dedicated pool defaults to "no shaping" at the pool egress level; we only have tenant-level policers for hosted. dedicated was assumed "isolated" so we let bursts through.

priya: cost note: cross-az transfers + cloud egress for those bursts pushed bill for eu-west up. rough hit ~ $750 for the window (estimate).

dan: proposal: implement "egress shepherding" — token-bucket per-pool with a configurable steady rate, short burst allowance, and an exponential backoff when queueing detected. preserve pinned tenant SLA by allowing short bursts but throttle sustained drains.

ashley: also propose a routing tweak: large-response routing preference -> prefer same-AZ dedicated slices or local caching. avoid cross-AZ transfer when possible.

samir: caveat: dedicated customers buy isolation. adding pool-level shaping could be perceived as degrading guarantees. we need opt-in or clear contract change.

lee: rollout idea: start with telemetry + dry-run enforcement (log-only) for 48h to collect egress_backpressure events and false-positives. then opt-in beta, then wider.

dan: I'll sketch the config shape in a PR: fields like `egress_limit_bytes_per_sec`, `burst_multiplier`, `grace_period_s`. include a `mode: dry-run|enforce|off` flag.

ashley: add these metrics: `pool.egress.rate`, `pool.egress.burst_used`, `pool.egress.backpressure_events{tenant}`, and an alert if backpressure_events > 5% of requests over 5m.

samir: longer-term: API-level mitigation — if predicted response > 100MB, suggest streaming + multipart upload or push to customer-managed S3. autoprompt clients to use `upload_url` flow instead of direct dump.

lee: also watch connection patterns: SSE or many small streams add up. we should enforce `max_conns_per_tenant` and aggregate egress accounting.

priya: operational ask: who owns the runbook update & customer comms? product + ops needed for SLA language and rollback plan.

ashley: I'll add a short runbook snippet under incidents/networking -> "egress shepherding" with detection queries and rollback steps.

dan: infra tasks I will take: (1) dry-run token-bucket implementation in edge-proxy, (2) telemetry hooks + logs, (3) config PR for pool schema. target: dry-run by Friday.

samir: product action: craft a customer-facing note for dedicated customers explaining optional shaping and opt-in beta. highlight that shaping prevents neighbor-induced ToR saturation and keeps overall latency stable.

infra-bot: probe-job launched: egress-probe-runner in prod-eu sampling 1m windows for 6h.

priya: ok — blockers? legal/finance ok with communication cost numbers?

ashley: finance ready for an initial estimate. legal flagged SLA wording; will coordinate with product.

dan: timeline summary: dry-run telemetry by Fri, opt-in beta next week, enforcement tentative after validation. If anyone objects to plan, speak now.

samir: +1. start with log-only so we can tune thresholds. :+1:

lee: noted — I'll add conn-limit metrics and a dashboard tile.

ashley: thanks everyone. follow-ups: dan will open PR and samir will draft customer note. I'll update runbook.

priya: closing loop — will schedule a 30m sync on Thurs if needed.

ashley: closing thread for now, keep updates in the PR.
